extracted.intended_audience: legislators, statesmen, financiers, and informed readers of political economy
extracted.subtask_description: Normative criteria and practical requirements for sound public finance and fiscal governance as argued in a political-essay context, aimed at evaluating the conduct of legislators and financiers (taxation, revenue, credit, confiscation, and public expenditures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Importance of state revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: The revenue of the state is the state. In effect, all depends upon it, whether for support or for reformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revenue is the spring of all power and the means by which public virtue, magnanimity, beneficence, fortitude, and the tutelary protection of the arts are sustained; without a just revenue the body politic cannot display collective virtue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core objects of a financier
rubrics_metrics.description: The objects of a financier are, then, to secure an ample revenue; to impose it with judgment and equality; to employ it economically; and when necessity obliges him to make use of credit, to secure its foundations in that instance, and forever, by the clearness and candor of his proceedings, the exactness of his calculations, and the solidity of his funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate finance managers against these four tasks (securing revenue, equitable imposition, economy of spending, and prudent, transparent use of credit); failure in any undermines state strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impose taxes with judgment and equality
rubrics_metrics.description: To impose [revenue] with judgment and equality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid ad hoc exemptions or letting districts decide what to withhold; ensure distribution of tax burden proportional to means so that productive capital isn't disproportionately taxed; otherwise new inequalities and oppression arise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ public money economically; scrutinize state expenses
rubrics_metrics.description: To employ [revenue] economically; reduce prodigal expenses and examine costs of the Assembly, municipalities, armies, police, pension-lists, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Economy must include the expenditures of the new authorities themselves; comparing former and present expenses against the current state of the treasury is necessary to judge real economy versus mere posturing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not rely on voluntary benevolence or patriotic donations as revenue
rubrics_metrics.description: Voluntary benevolence (a fourth of income 'estimated on the honor') and patriotic donations are weak, ineffective, unequal, and cannot replace regular revenue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat such measures as temporary, unreliable, and likely to concentrate burdens on the virtuous and productive; they are politically and fiscally unsound and should not be counted on for serious fiscal planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain and build public credit on real backing and convertibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Paper money is of value in commerce because in law it is of none; our paper is of value because it originates in cash actually deposited and is convertible at pleasure into cash.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public credit requires that paper circulation be founded on real deposits or assets and be freely convertible; coercive acceptance or legal fiat without backing destroys external confidence and credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and authentic valuation when using confiscated property as security
rubrics_metrics.description: When the Assembly appropriated Church lands as security it pledged to show distinctly the expense of religious establishments and to make the estates 'disengaged of all charges' and to determine the sum necessary for the year; they ought to furnish a rent-roll or inventory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before treating confiscated property as a fund, publish authenticated valuations, inventories, and statements of encumbrances and charges so purchasers and creditors know exactly what they are buying and to preserve public faith.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper procedure for establishing a land-bank/assignats
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish a land-bank one should ascertain the gross value of the estate, charges of management and disposition, incumbrances, strike a net surplus (the only security), vest it in trustees, indicate parcels and conditions of sale, and permit creditors to subscribe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceed 'like men of business' — methodically and rationally — so the dealer knows exactly what he purchases and to reduce the risk of bankruptcy that commonly follows ill-designed land-banks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not destroy settled revenue expecting to rebuild from confiscation
rubrics_metrics.description: Who but the most desperate adventurers could have thought of destroying the settled revenue of the state, the sole security for the public credit, in the hope of rebuilding it with the materials of confiscated property?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid substituting perennial revenue sources for one-off confiscations; confiscation cannot reliably substitute for a settled tax base and undermines long-term credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid issuing paper (assignats) without clear, sufficient security
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue of assignats forced on the people left wants of the state as urgent; old assignats depreciated and the remedy was to issue more assignats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Issuing increasing quantities of paper without solid security leads to depreciation, loss of public confidence, and perverse effects (collectors taking specie and accounting in depreciated paper). Do not treat issuance as a mechanical cure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure collectors and treasury transact in specie or equivalent reliable value
rubrics_metrics.description: If collectors receive coin, they should pay the treasury in specie; accounting in depreciated paper while receiving coin yields profits to collectors and losses to the Treasury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain rules that prevent arbitrage by collectors (receiving specie but remitting depreciated paper) — otherwise the treasury loses value and credit is undermined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid coercion to force acceptance of paper currency
rubrics_metrics.description: They drive, by the point of the bayonets, their slaves ... to take their fictions for currencies, and to swallow down paper pills by thirty-four millions sterling at a dose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Credit founded on force is counterfeit; compelled acceptance of unbacked paper will not create genuine credit or commerce and will damage domestic and international confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not conceal existing charges when assigning confiscated estates
rubrics_metrics.description: Every deficiency in the general and municipal establishments becomes a charge on the confiscated estate; they have purposely covered what they ought to have cleared with a thick fog.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full disclosure of municipal and other charges that attach to seized property is necessary; otherwise the supposed security is illusory and will not answer mortgages or sustain public credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Account honestly for the costs of maintaining religion and pensions when sequestrating church property
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee report shows that charges for keeping up religious establishments and pensions exceeded the income of the acquired estates by two millions sterling annually, besides a debt of seven millions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When confiscating church/property to support the state, the legislature must include in public accounts the real costs they promised to defray (support of ministers, relief of the poor, pensions) or they break faith and ruin credit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of fiscal expedients and mercantile contrivances exalted into policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawing and re-drawing, circulation for putting off the evil day, play between the Treasury and the Caisse d'Escompte, old exploded contrivances of mercantile fraud exalted into policy are unworthy: the revenue will not be trifled with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid short-term contrivances and mercantile tricks masquerading as policy; these may postpone problems but will not substitute for sound, perennial fiscal design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exercise prudence when recommending or defending new financial schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: When Necker expressed apprehension for what was to succeed, instead of entering into the grounds to prevent the prognosticated evil, he received a friendly reprimand; ministers must explore and prevent predicted financial ills.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Officials should investigate and act on credible financial warnings rather than suppressing or ignoring them; transparent analysis and remedial planning are required to avert collapse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not substitute sacrilege or plunder for sound fiscal policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Their fanatical confidence in the omnipotence of Church plunder has induced these philosophers to overlook care of the public estate; 'this universal medicine made of Church mummy is to cure all the evils of the state.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confiscation as a general remedy is illusory; policy should not rest on moralistic or ideological assumptions that plunder will replenish the state — assess sustainability and consequences first.
